notes.text: The book is cut to the new shape and the plugs, sites, worlds and the door are written in, much of it still marked as assumption. The real contracts run in the repository. The spike that proves the door and the clock is running. Three things wait on Aaron: equity, the payroll route, and the AWS sign-in for the machine.
Done now also means a shared world running a thin line through the whole stack on the machine. That needs Aaron's AWS sign-in, the subdomain and the DNS records before it can start.

The plan page is live and is now where the work is tracked. Four things wait on Aaron: the AWS sign-in with the subdomain and DNS records, the cost audit's switch-offs, equity, and the payroll filing route. The door and clock spike and the contracts' deeper tests are still running.

The plan now explains itself: an outline, and a page for every milestone and task. Everything that waits on Aaron is in one list on the Questions page, and his answers are saved to plan/answers.jsonl on this Mac. The door, the recorder, the clock and snapshots are built on the test sites; the coordinator is re-running their checks before closing that task.

Aaron answered every question. Six are accepted. Seasons are dropped for now. Payroll targets the United States first. The clock question is open again: he wants to understand what can go wrong, and a study is being written.

10 November 2026 (coordinator): the clock is settled: Aaron accepted the recommendation, option A of the time study, and the book records it with six tests (m1-time-proof, first on the path). The spikes' evidence is in the book. The jurisdiction is open again: Aaron left it open, preferring a crypto-friendly place (the UAE a candidate), so payroll waits on a comparison of places (m1-payroll-uk).
